notes: This is an upright handwritten mathematical page with manuscript number 40 in a circle at its upper left, display numbers (105), (106), (107), internal references to (103) and (105), and pale lower-left pencil foliation 81. No date is present.

The author says the underlines for MD-graphs have been dropped. His original longer explanation replacing Pi(M, Gamma) with lighter Pi M notation is entirely cancelled; de = is the written abbreviation and has not been expanded in the transcription.

Above the original cancelled phrase tire de (105), the author first inserted a défini and cancelled it too; retrouve is the final uncancelled replacement, farther to the right on that higher baseline. The sequential editorial state is encoded explicitly.

The running prose describes the object of (106) as a 2-cartesian product in (105), then as a connected groupoid and an extension by twisted integer modules. It asserts a combined kernel with exponent C amalg C prime. These are the page's claims, not assertions verified by this first reading.

The live second index in (106) is G double-prime. A third index was cancelled. The double-prime preference within that cancelled index is a low-confidence visual reading, not a reconstruction from the mathematics.

The three ext. abbreviations have a c-like open e and a very compact crossed x, accounting for H's cat. readings. The visible word extension later on the same page provides an internal comparison; no theorem or unseen page was used to fix the reading.

The explanatory formula beneath the right middle object of (105) visibly has two opening parentheses and one closing parenthesis. The draft preserves that source imbalance. Both witnesses add an outer closing parenthesis.

The long upper curve of (105) has a visible intermediate arrowhead as well as its final head. Both slanting braces and their annotations are retained. The draft uses standard TikZ-cd labels as a graphical approximation for the brace shapes and the intermediate head; no TeX compilation was performed.
The extreme-right le in the introduction of (107) has a retraced lower stroke. I have not asserted a separate underline, because the loop and return may belong to the letter formation itself.

Two isolated horizontal pen strokes below/right of (105) have no clear linguistic or mathematical attachment. Their shapes are preserved in a small TikZ margin drawing without interpreting them as an equation or punctuation.

Cancelled indices and the crossed fragment beneath (105) remain genuinely uncertain. No cancelled letter was regularized on mathematical grounds. No OCR, external research, source outside the assigned packet, or TeX compilation was used.

After the main reader independently inspected the same crops, all four Z occurrences are encoded as \mathbb Z: their doubled diagonal strokes are visible on the source. This is an alphabet/form correction, not a change to the claimed groups.
